title: mol-apicity-release
description:
Apicity npm release formula — cut a release of @apicity/* packages from the
`stable` branch to the npm registry.

Branch model:
  - main   = agents work here (feature work lands here first)
  - stable = release branch; releases cut from stable; tags pushed to stable

The formula publishes 15 scoped packages in one go: 14 providers under
packages/provider/* plus packages/mcp-server. All ship under one version
and one dist-tag (alpha / beta / next / latest).

This formula does NOT auto-publish without authentication. The `publish`
step requires an authenticated `npm whoami` and (most likely) an interactive
2FA OTP. The human running the agent must be present at that step.

## Variables

| Variable     | Source | Default | Description                                    |
|--------------|--------|---------|------------------------------------------------|
| version      | caller | —       | Semver to publish, e.g. 0.1.0-alpha.1          |
| dist_tag     | caller | alpha   | npm dist-tag (alpha / beta / next / latest)    |
| dry_run      | caller | false   | If "true", stop after publish-dry-run          |
| release_bead | caller | —       | Tracking bead this release closes              |

title: Publish to npm
description:
**HUMAN MUST BE PRESENT.** This step requires an authenticated npm session
and (most likely) an interactive 2FA one-time password.

**1. Verify auth:**
```bash
npm whoami   # MUST print the publishing account
npm config get registry   # should be https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

If `npm whoami` errors, STOP. Run `npm login` interactively first.

**2. Publish all 15 packages:**
```bash
pnpm -r --filter "@apicity/*" publish --tag alpha --no-git-checks
```

`pnpm` will pause on each package for the OTP prompt if 2FA is enabled.
Type the code from your authenticator. `--no-git-checks` is required because
we're publishing from a release commit that may not yet have an upstream tag
(the `tag-and-push` step handles that next).

**3. Verify on the registry:**
```bash
npm view @apicity/openai dist-tags    # expect alpha: 0.1.0-alpha.0
npm view @apicity/mcp-server dist-tags
```

If publish fails partway through (network, auth lapse), some packages may
already be live. STOP. Resume by re-running `pnpm publish` for only the
packages that didn't get through — npm rejects re-publishing the same
version, so it's safe to retry the whole filter.

**Exit criteria:** All 15 packages visible at `0.1.0-alpha.0` under `alpha`.

```bash

```

```bash

git branch -D "$BRANCH"              # Branch is pushed; refinery owns it now
```

```bash
gc bd update ac-ckcj --set-metadata target=main --notes "Implemented: <brief summary>"
```
Branch was recorded in workspace-setup and is already in metadata.
This adds the target for the refinery. If an existing pull request was
provided by the caller, `metadata.existing_pr` is preserved for refinery
validation. The refinery records canonical `pr_url` only after verifying
the PR is open and matches the branch, base, and origin repository.

**5. Reassign to refinery:**
```bash
REFINERY_TARGET="${GC_RIG:+$GC_RIG/}{{binding_prefix}}refinery"
gc bd update ac-ckcj --status=open --assignee="$REFINERY_TARGET" --set-metadata gc.routed_to="$REFINERY_TARGET"
```

`${GC_RIG:+$GC_RIG/}{{binding_prefix}}refinery` resolves to
`$GC_RIG/{{binding_prefix}}refinery` when running inside a rig session,
or `{{binding_prefix}}refinery` when running in an HQ-only city where
the workspace is the rig. Writing a rendered empty rig prefix produces
`/{{binding_prefix}}refinery` and strands beads outside the refinery pool.

Update both `assignee` AND `gc.routed_to` so the reconciler stops
counting this bead for the polecat pool and starts counting it for
the refinery pool. Without updating `gc.routed_to`, the reconciler
spawns phantom polecats that can't claim the bead.

The refinery will pick this up, rebase onto main, run tests,
merge, and close the bead. If there's a conflict, the refinery puts the
bead back in the pool with `rejection_reason` metadata — a new polecat
picks it up and resumes from the existing branch.

**6. Signal reconciler and exit.**
```bash
gc runtime drain-ack
exit
```

`gc runtime drain-ack` tells the reconciler to kill this session. The
reconciler only restarts you if the pool check command finds more work.
You are GONE. Done means gone. There is no idle state.

**Exit criteria:** Branch pushed, metadata set, bead reassigned, drain acknowledged, session exited.

title: mol-polecat-work
description:
Polecat work lifecycle — feature-branch variant.

Extends mol-polecat-base with feature-branch workspace setup and
refinery-based submission. The polecat creates a feature branch,
implements the work, then pushes and reassigns to the refinery for

1. Receive work (molecule poured with this formula, assigned to you)
2. Follow steps in order (read descriptions, execute, move to next)
3. Submit: push branch, set metadata on work bead, assign to refinery, exit
4. You are GONE — Refinery merges, closes the bead

The polecat sets `metadata.branch` and `metadata.target` on the work bead
and reassigns it to the refinery. The refinery merges and closes.

|-----------|--------|

| Blocked on external | Mail Witness, mark yourself stuck |
| Context filling | `gc runtime request-restart` (blocks until controller kills you) |
| Unsure what to do | Mail Witness, don't guess |

description:
Prepare release artifacts (READMEs + CHANGELOGs + npm metadata) so apicity is publish-ready. This is documentation/metadata prep only — do NOT cut the release, run `mol-apicity-release`, or push tags.

## Context

Apicity is a pnpm monorepo of 15 scoped npm packages (14 providers under `packages/provider/*` plus `packages/mcp-server`) shipped in lockstep. No git tags exist yet — this is preparation for the **first** release. Read `RELEASE.md` for the existing release process and branch model (`main` → `stable` → publish under `alpha` dist-tag for pre-1.0).

## Current state (as of audit time)

- ✓ Root: `README.md`, `RELEASE.md`, `LICENSE`, `package.json` (version `1.0.0` — note: this disagrees with RELEASE.md's pre-1.0 alpha plan; resolve as part of this work)
- ✓ Each of 15 packages has a `README.md` and `LICENSE`
- ✗ No `CHANGELOG.md` anywhere (root or per-package)
- ✓ Per-package `package.json` exists for every package

## Scope

### 1. Root CHANGELOG.md
Create `/CHANGELOG.md` at the repo root following Keep a Changelog format (https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). Seed with an `[Unreleased]` section plus an inaugural release section once the version is decided. Capture meaningful work items by walking `git log --oneline` — group by Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed.

### 2. Per-package CHANGELOG.md
Each of the 15 packages needs its own `CHANGELOG.md` (npm shows these on the package page):
- `packages/mcp-server/CHANGELOG.md`
- `packages/provider/{openai,xai,fal,kimicoding,kie,anthropic,fireworks,alibaba,elevenlabs,free-media-upload,x,meta,polymarket,cost}/CHANGELOG.md`

Format: same Keep a Changelog template. For first release, just an `[Unreleased]` placeholder is fine — they'll all bump together.

### 3. Audit each package README.md (15 of them)
For every package's `README.md`, verify it has:
- Install snippet (`pnpm add @apicity/<name>` and `npm i @apicity/<name>`)
- One-line description matching the `description` field in its `package.json`
- Minimal usage example that compiles
- Link back to the monorepo (https://github.com/justintanner/apicity)
- Reference to the LICENSE
Update any package READMEs that are missing or stale on these points. Do NOT rewrite working READMEs; this is gap-fill, not a rewrite.

### 4. Audit each package.json for npm publishability
For every package's `package.json`, verify these fields are present and correct (npm requires/recommends them for publish):
- `name`, `version`, `description`, `license`, `author`/`contributors` (optional), `repository` (with `directory` pointing to the package path), `homepage`, `bugs`, `keywords`, `main`, `types`, `exports`, `files`, `publishConfig.access` (probably `public` for scoped packages)
- Most importantly: `version` must be **the same** across ALL packages (lockstep is enforced by the release formula)

Report any drift between packages and propose a single target version. If you find a clear inconsistency between root `package.json` (`1.0.0`) and `RELEASE.md` (alpha track), follow RELEASE.md's policy — it is the source of truth. Pick a sensible first-release version like `0.1.0-alpha.0` unless the user has signaled otherwise on the bead.

### 5. Root README spot-check (do NOT rewrite)
Confirm the root `README.md` references all 15 packages, points users at the right install commands, and accurately describes the monorepo. Fix only stale facts.

## Out of scope

- Running `mol-apicity-release`, `pnpm publish`, or pushing tags
- Bumping `version` in any `package.json` (other than reconciling drift; do NOT pick a new version number unilaterally — leave the version-bump to the release formula)

if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH"; then
    if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH"; then

        git merge --ff-only "origin/$BRANCH" || {

            echo "STOP. Reconcile the branch before continuing."

    fi
elif git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH"; then

    exit 1

Ensure you have an isolated git worktree and a clean feature branch.
Every check is idempotent — safe to re-run after crash/restart.

**Config: base_branch = main**
**Config: setup_command = **

`main` is resolved by `gc sling` in this order:
1. `metadata.target` on the work bead
2. `metadata.target` on the parent convoy chain
3. the rig repo's default branch

**1. Fetch latest:**
```bash
git fetch --prune origin
```

**2. Ensure worktree exists.**

Check if `metadata.work_dir` already records your worktree path:
```bash
WORKTREE=$(gc bd show ac-f3gp --json | jq -r '.[0].metadata.work_dir // empty')
```

**If worktree path exists in metadata** — reuse it:
```bash
cd "$WORKTREE"              # Enter existing worktree
```
If the directory is missing (witness cleaned it, disk issue), fall through
to create a new one.

**If no worktree** — create one scoped to the bead, not the agent:
```bash
WORKTREE_PATH=$(pwd)/worktrees/ac-f3gp
git worktree add "$WORKTREE_PATH" --detach origin/main
cd "$WORKTREE_PATH"
```
Record immediately so restarts and witness recovery can find it:
```bash
gc bd update ac-f3gp --set-metadata work_dir="$WORKTREE_PATH"
```

Worktrees are scoped to the work bead (not the agent name) so that:
- An agent can pick up new work even if an old worktree is being recovered
- Multiple orphaned worktrees can coexist without collision
- The witness cleans them independently per-bead

**3. Ensure branch exists.**

Check if `metadata.branch` already records a branch:
```bash
BRANCH=$(gc bd show ac-f3gp --json | jq -r '.[0].metadata.branch // empty')
```

**If branch exists in metadata** — treat it as authoritative. This
metadata may come from rejection recovery or from a caller that wants
work applied to an existing branch. Fetch the named remote branch first.
If `origin/$BRANCH` exists, make the local branch fast-forward to that
remote tip or stop on divergence:
```bash
git fetch origin "+refs/heads/$BRANCH:refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH" || echo "Could not fetch metadata.branch=$BRANCH from origin. Checking local refs before stopping."
if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH"; then
    if git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH"; then
        git checkout "$BRANCH" || exit 1
        git merge --ff-only "origin/$BRANCH" || {
            echo "Local branch $BRANCH diverged from origin/$BRANCH."
            echo "STOP. Reconcile the branch before continuing."
            gc runtime drain-ack
            exit 1
        }
    else
        git checkout --track -b "$BRANCH" "origin/$BRANCH" || exit 1
    fi
elif git show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH"; then
    git checkout "$BRANCH" || exit 1
else
    echo "metadata.branch=$BRANCH was set but no local or origin branch exists."
    echo "STOP. Do not create a different branch."
    gc runtime drain-ack
    exit 1
fi
```
If resuming a rejected branch, rebase onto latest base:
```bash
REJECTION=$(gc bd show ac-f3gp --json | jq -r '.[0].metadata.rejection_reason // empty')
if [ -n "$REJECTION" ]; then
    git rebase origin/main
    # If conflicts: resolve them (this is likely the rejection reason)
    # After resolving: git rebase --continue
    gc bd update ac-f3gp --unset-metadata rejection_reason
fi
```

**If no branch** — create one and record it:
```bash
BRANCH="polecat/ac-f3gp"
git checkout -b "$BRANCH" origin/main
gc bd update ac-f3gp --set-metadata branch="$BRANCH"
```

Recording the branch early means:
- Witness can find and salvage your work if you crash
- Rejection-aware resume knows which branch to check out
- The submit step updates the metadata (branch may change after rebase)

```bash
git status                  # Should be clean
```

**5. Run project setup (if configured):**
```bash

```

on latest main, deps installed, worktree and branch recorded
on the bead.

title: Submit work to refinery and exit
description:
Hand off your work and self-clean. You cease to exist after this step.

**1. Final clean-state verification (safeguard):**
```bash
git status --porcelain
```
If ANY output (untracked files, uncommitted changes):
```bash
git add -A && git commit -m "chore: capture remaining work (ac-b6v)"
```
This is a belt-and-suspenders check — self-review should have caught this,
but we never push with untracked work left behind.

**2. Push your branch:**
```bash
git push origin HEAD
```

**3. Clean up local branch (prevent stale branch accumulation):**
```bash
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current)
git checkout --detach                 # Detach so we can delete the branch
git branch -D "$BRANCH"              # Branch is pushed; refinery owns it now
```

**4. Update metadata on the work bead:**
```bash
gc bd update ac-b6v --set-metadata target=main --notes "Implemented: <brief summary>"
```
Branch was recorded in workspace-setup and is already in metadata.
This adds the target for the refinery. If an existing pull request was
provided by the caller, `metadata.existing_pr` is preserved for refinery
validation. The refinery records canonical `pr_url` only after verifying
the PR is open and matches the branch, base, and origin repository.

**5. Reassign to refinery:**
```bash
REFINERY_TARGET="${GC_RIG:+$GC_RIG/}gastown.refinery"
gc bd update ac-b6v --status=open --assignee="$REFINERY_TARGET" --set-metadata gc.routed_to="$REFINERY_TARGET"
```

`${GC_RIG:+$GC_RIG/}gastown.refinery` resolves to
`$GC_RIG/gastown.refinery` when running inside a rig session,
or `gastown.refinery` when running in an HQ-only city where
the workspace is the rig. Writing a rendered empty rig prefix produces
`/gastown.refinery` and strands beads outside the refinery pool.

Update both `assignee` AND `gc.routed_to` so the reconciler stops
counting this bead for the polecat pool and starts counting it for
the refinery pool. Without updating `gc.routed_to`, the reconciler
spawns phantom polecats that can't claim the bead.

The refinery will pick this up, rebase onto main, run tests,
merge, and close the bead. If there's a conflict, the refinery puts the
bead back in the pool with `rejection_reason` metadata — a new polecat
picks it up and resumes from the existing branch.

**6. Signal reconciler and exit.**
```bash
gc runtime drain-ack
exit
```

`gc runtime drain-ack` tells the reconciler to kill this session. The
reconciler only restarts you if the pool check command finds more work.
You are GONE. Done means gone. There is no idle state.

**Exit criteria:** Branch pushed, metadata set, bead reassigned, drain acknowledged, session exited.

description:
Do the actual implementation work.

**Working principles:**
- Follow existing codebase conventions
- Make atomic, focused commits
- Keep changes scoped to the assigned issue
- Don't gold-plate or scope-creep

**If resuming a rejected branch:** Read `metadata.rejection_reason`
from load-context. Focus on fixing the specific issue that caused
rejection — don't redo everything.

**Commit frequently:**
```bash
git add <files>
git commit -m "<type>: <description> (ac-b6v)"
```

Commit types: feat, fix, refactor, test, docs, chore

**Discovered work (outside scope):**
```bash
bd create --title "Found: <description>" --type bug --priority 2
```
Do NOT fix unrelated issues in this branch.

**If stuck (>15 minutes):**
```bash
gc mail send <rig>/witness -s "HELP: Stuck on implementation" -m "Issue: ac-b6v
Problem: <what's blocking you>
Tried: <what you've attempted>"
```

**If context filling up:**
```bash
gc runtime request-restart
```
This blocks until the controller kills your session. The next session
resumes from context (re-reads formula steps, checks git/bead state).

**Exit criteria:** Implementation complete, all changes committed.

title: mol-polecat-work
description:
Polecat work lifecycle — feature-branch variant.

Extends mol-polecat-base with feature-branch workspace setup and
refinery-based submission. The polecat creates a feature branch,
implements the work, then pushes and reassigns to the refinery for
merge review.

## Polecat Contract (Self-Cleaning Model)

1. Receive work (molecule poured with this formula, assigned to you)
2. Follow steps in order (read descriptions, execute, move to next)
3. Submit: push branch, set metadata on work bead, assign to refinery, exit
4. You are GONE — Refinery merges, closes the bead

**No MR beads.** Work beads flow directly: pool → polecat → refinery → closed.
The polecat sets `metadata.branch` and `metadata.target` on the work bead
and reassigns it to the refinery. The refinery merges and closes.
`main` may come from the work bead's own `metadata.target` or
be inherited from a parent convoy with `metadata.target` set.

**Rejection-aware.** If the work bead has `metadata.branch` and
`metadata.rejection_reason`, a previous attempt was rejected by the
refinery. Resume the existing branch — don't redo all the work.

## Failure Modes

| Situation | Action |
|-----------|--------|
| Tests fail | Fix them. Do not proceed with failures. |
| Blocked on external | Mail Witness, mark yourself stuck |
| Context filling | `gc runtime request-restart` (blocks until controller kills you) |
| Unsure what to do | Mail Witness, don't guess |

Find every test currently skipped, xfailed, or otherwise not running, and resolve each one. Decision rule per test:

1. If it tests code that no longer exists, delete the test (and any orphan fixtures).
2. If it was skipped due to a known fixed bug, unskip and run it.

- Commit per directory with a message describing what was removed/unskipped and why.
- Do NOT mass-delete files without reading them. Each removal should be justified in the commit body.

title: mol-refinery-patrol
description:
Refinery patrol loop. Poured as a root-only wisp on startup:

  gc bd mol wisp mol-refinery-patrol --root-only --var target_branch=main --var rig_name=ac --var binding_prefix=gastown.
  gc bd update $WISP --assignee=$GC_AGENT

Each wisp is ONE iteration: check for work, merge one branch, pour
the next iteration. On crash, re-read the formula steps and determine
where you left off from context (git state, bead state, last action).

Formula steps are NOT materialized as child beads. Read the step
descriptions below and work through them in order.

The loop mechanism: every exit path (happy or early) pours the next
wisp before burning this one. The prompt only bootstraps the first wisp.

Work beads flow directly: pool → polecat → refinery → closed.
No separate MR beads. The polecat sets metadata (branch, target) on
the work bead and assigns it to the refinery. On rejection, the
refinery puts the bead back in the pool with rejection metadata.

Merge strategy is per-work-bead metadata:
- `direct` (default): fast-forward merge to target and push
- `mr` / `pr`: publish a GitHub pull request instead of landing directly

In `mr` mode, refinery treats PR publication as the terminal handoff for
the direct-bead workflow: it records the PR URL on the work bead and
closes the bead once the PR is verified.

Read each step's description before acting — Config values override defaults.
